This is contrary to the apparent meaning, and upon it the ruling would be general, but there is discussion about it.

Ibn Jarir and others narrated from Ibn Zayd that the ruling of the verse applied when Islam was small in number; then when it grew and spread, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾. You know that Islam had spread when this surah was revealed. There is no hiding what the verse contains of allusion to those who stayed behind out of desire for pleasures and inclination toward desires, not caring about what he, peace and blessings be upon him, endured. A group had indeed stayed behind from him, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, as you know for that reason. It has been reported that some Muslims stayed behind, then some of them regretted it and disliked their position, and so they caught up with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, not concerned by hardships, like Abu Khaythamah. It was narrated that "he, may Allah be pleased with him, reached his orchard, and he had a beautiful wife who spread for him in the shade, spread the mat for him, and brought him dates and cool water. He looked and said: 'Cool shade, ripe dates, cold water, and a beautiful woman, while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, is in the heat and the wind. This is not a good place to stay,' so he saddled his she-camel, took his sword and spear, and set off like the wind. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, cast his glance toward the road, and behold, a rider appeared to him through the mirage. Peace and blessings be upon him said: 'Be Abu Khaythamah,' and so he was. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, rejoiced at him and asked forgiveness for him."

﴿That﴾ is a reference to what the speech indicates of the obligation of accompanying him, ﴿because﴾, that is, by reason of the fact that ﴿they are not afflicted with thirst﴾, that is, any part of thirst, and it has been read with the long and short vowel forms, ﴿nor fatigue﴾, nor weariness, whatever it may be, ﴿nor hunger﴾, nor famine, whatever it may be, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, in the struggle against His enemies, or in His obedience, glorified is He, in general. ﴿Nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers﴾, that is, that angers them and constricts their chests. The word (waṭʾ) means treading with the feet or the like, such as the hooves of horses. It may also be interpreted as attacking and fighting. From it is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace: "The last trampling that Allah trampled was at Wadj." The word (mawṭiʾ) is, according to the most well-known and apparent view, a noun of place. The subject of ﴿yaghīẓu﴾ is its pronoun, with an omitted term: "their treading enrages," because the place itself does not enrage. It may also be a pronoun referring back to
[p. 47]
the treading that is implied in it. If (mawṭiʾ) is taken as a verbal noun, like (mawrid), then the matter is clear. ﴿Nor do they gain from an enemy any gain﴾, that is, they do not take anything of taking. It is a verbal noun like "killing" and "capture." The verb is (nāla yanīlu), and it has been said: (nāla yanūlu), so the origin of (naylan) is (nawlan), and the waw was changed to a yā' contrary to analogy. It may also mean "what is taken," in which case it is an object of (yanālūna), meaning they do not gain anything of things ﴿except that a righteous deed is written for them thereby﴾, that is, by the aforementioned, which is all that has preceded. Therefore the pronoun is singular. It may also refer to each one of these individually, as alternatives. Al-Nasafi said: "He made the pronoun singular because, when the particle (lā) was repeated, each of them became, as an alternative, singled out for mention and intended by the promise." For this reason our jurists said: if someone swears he will not eat bread or meat, he breaks the oath by either one of them; but if he swears he will not eat meat and bread, he does not break it except by combining both. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to ﴿thirst﴾ and what is conjoined to it: that is, no thirst afflicts them, nor anything of that sort, except that it is written for them thereby as ﴿a righteous deed﴾, that is, the reward of that. The speech therefore has an omitted term, and it may be taken as a metonymy for the reward, and it was interpreted as such because it is the intended purpose of writing deeds. The tanwīn is for magnification. The meaning is that they deserve that with a necessary entitlement by the force of His promise, the Exalted, not by any obligation upon Him, glorified is He.

The verse has been cited as evidence that whoever intends good, his striving in it is thanked, whether by standing, sitting, walking, speaking, or otherwise; and as evidence that a reinforcement shares in the spoils with the army after the end of the battle, because treading their lands is among what enrages them. The Prophet, may Allah exalt him and grant him peace, indeed gave a share to the two sons of ʿĀmir when they arrived after the war had ended. Abu Hanifah, may Allah exalt him, cited it, as al-Jalal al-Suyuti reported, as evidence for the permissibility of fornication with the women of the people of war in the land of war. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾ 120, for their good-doing. The clause is in the position of a reason for the writing. By "the good-doers" is meant either those under discussion, and placing the apparent noun in place of the pronoun serves to praise them, to attest that they are included among the good-doers, and that their deeds are of the category of good-doing, and to indicate that the ground for the ruling is the cause; or it refers to the category in general, and they are included in it as a primary inclusion.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 121:

﴿And they spend no expenditure, small﴾ even a date or the lash of a whip, ﴿nor large﴾ as ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) spent in the army of hardship (jaysh al-ʿusrah). The mention of "large" after "small," although the reward for the first is known to include the reward for the second, is because the intended meaning is generalization (al-taʿmim), not the specific items mentioned, since the meaning is: "they spend nothing whatsoever." So it should not be imagined that the apparent sense is the reverse. In Irshad al-Aql al-Salim, it is said that the order is based on how frequently each occurs and how rarely, and the insertion of wa (and) and la (not) serves to specify that each of them is independently recorded in the books and rewarded, not to emphasize the negation, as in the statement of Allah, exalted is His majesty: ﴿And they do not cross﴾, meaning: they do not pass over in their journey for a raid ﴿a valley﴾ (wadiyan). It is originally an active participle from wadiya, meaning it flowed, so it means the flood itself. Then it became common for its place, which is the winding passage among mountains and hills where water flows, and then it became literally applied to any land. It is pluralized as awdiyah, like nad becoming andiyah and naj becoming anjiyah, and there is no fourth such pattern in Arabic speech, as has been said. ﴿except that it is written for them﴾, meaning: it is recorded for them, or written in the scrolls or the Preserved Tablet. The word "kutiba" should not be interpreted as "prescribed as an entitlement," because of the causal clause that follows. The pronoun in ﴿kutiba﴾ follows the pattern of what preceded, meaning: "what is mentioned," or "each one of them." It has been said that it refers to the deed, but this is not correct. This clause was separated and placed at the end because it is easier than what came before it. ﴿so that Allah may reward them﴾ for that ﴿with the best of what they used to do﴾, meaning: the best reward of their deeds, in the sense that their deeds have a good reward and a better one, and He, glorified is He, has chosen for them the best reward.

The accusative of ﴿best﴾ is as a verbal noun (maṣdar), since it is attached to an omitted verbal noun.

Al-Imam said: In this there are two views. The first is that "the best" is an attribute of their deed, and in it are the obligatory, the recommended and the permissible; so He rewards them for the first two but not the last. The apparent reading is that the accusative of "best" is then a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from the pronoun in "yajziyahum," as has been said. It was objected that this is remote from the context, with little benefit, since its sum is that He rewards them for the obligatory and the recommended, and that what is mentioned of it... its weakness is not hidden, and that it is not hidden to anyone. Its being a metaphor for pardon of what they committed of shortcomings within it, if it occurs, since restricting the reward to it suggests that they are not rewarded for other than it, which contradicts the apparent sense. Then he said: The second is that "the best" is an attribute of the reward, meaning: that He may reward them with a reward that is better than their deeds and superior, and it is the thawab (reward). Abu Hayyan objected to it: if "the best" is an attribute of the reward, how can it be attached to the deeds when it is not a part of them, and how is it preferred over them without "min" (than)? There is no way to answer this by saying that the original is "mimma kanu..." so the deletion of "min" with the meaning remaining as it is, as has been said, because it yields this meaning.

The description of the expenditure as "small" and "large," rather than "few" and "many," although the intended meaning is that, has been said to be by analogy of obedience to disobedience, for they are described as "small" and "large" in their speech only, not as "few" and "many." So reflect.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 122:

﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together.﴾ That is, it was not proper for them to go out to the expedition (ghazw) all together. Al-Kalbi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that when Allah (exalted is He) imposed severity upon those who stayed behind, they said: "None of us shall ever stay behind from an army or a detachment." So they did this, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone, and the verse was revealed: ﴿It was not for the believers...﴾ and so on. The intent is a prohibition against their all going forth together (nafir), because of what this entails in terms of disrupting learning.

﴿Why should not a company from every division of them go forth?﴾ Here "lawla" is hortative (tahdiydiyya). With the past tense it expresses reproach for abandoning an action; with the present tense it expresses a request for it and a command to do it. However, reproach for abandoning something that can still be remedied may also convey a command to do it in the future. That is, "fa-hallā nafara" (so why did they not go forth?). ﴿From every division﴾ means from a large group, ﴿of them﴾ such as the people of a town or a great tribe, ﴿a company﴾ means a small group. Taking "firqa" and "ta'ifa" in this sense is derived from the context, and "min" here is partitive, because the part is usually fewer than the remainder. Otherwise, al-Jawhari did not distinguish between them. Some have mentioned that "ta'ifa" may apply to a single person, while others said it does not, and that its minimum is two; it has also been said three. ﴿That they may gain understanding in the religion﴾ means that they should undertake to acquire fiqh (understanding) in it. The verbal form "tafa''ala" indicates effort (takalluf), and its intended meaning is not the immediate sense, but rather enduring hardship in seeking it, because of its difficulty; it is not attained without zeal and striving. ﴿And that they may warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware.﴾ 122 That is, against what they are warned of. The pronouns in "yatafaqqahu" and "yundhiru" refer to the remaining division, which is understood from the speech. It has also been said that a supplement and an estimate are necessary, that is: "so why did not a company from every division go forth and a company remain behind, that they may gain understanding..." and so on.

It would seem more apparent to say "li-ya'lamu" instead of "li-yundhiru" and "yafqahuna" instead of "yahdharun." However, what is in the sublime composition was chosen to indicate that the aim of the teacher should be guidance and warning, and the aim of the student should be acquiring fear (of Allah), not expansiveness and arrogance.

Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali, may mercy be upon him, said: The name "fiqh" in the first era was a name for the knowledge of the Hereafter, knowledge of the subtleties of the afflictions of the souls and the corruptors of deeds, strong comprehension of the worthlessness of this world, intense longing for the bliss of the Hereafter, and the dominance of fear over the heart. This verse indicates it. So what is the basis of warning and intimidation is fiqh, not the definitions of divorce, li'an, salam, and leases. Farqad al-Sanji asked al-Hasan about something, and he answered him. He said: "Indeed the jurists disagree with you." Al-Hasan said: "May your mother be bereaved! Have you seen a jurist who helps you? Rather, the jurist is one who is detached from the world, desirous of the Hereafter, perceptive of his religion, persistent in worshipping his Lord, scrupulous, refraining from the honour of Muslims, chaste regarding their wealth, and sincere toward their community." He did not say in all of that "one who memorizes the branches of legal rulings." End quote. This is of great standing from al-Hasan. However, the common usage is to apply "faqih" to one who memorizes the branches (furu') absolutely, whether with their evidences or not, as in al-Tahrir. In al-Bahr, from al-Muntaqa, there is something agreeing with it. In al-Qunya, memorization together with the evidences is considered, so one who memorized without evidence does not enter into a bequest to "the jurists." From Abu Ja'far, he said: "The faqih among us is one who has reached the ultimate extent in fiqh, and one who is merely seeking fiqh is not a faqih, and he has no share of the bequest." The apparent view is that what is considered in bequests and the like is custom ('urf), which is what the statements of many of our companions require. Many have mentioned that the specification of warning in the mention is because it is the more important; otherwise the intent is comprehensive guidance, teaching the sunan, etiquette, obligations and permissible matters, and warning is more specific than it. The claim that the two are mutually entailed, so that mention of one suffices without the other, is heedlessness or inattention.

Many people went to the view that the intended "nafr" is going forth and departure in pursuit of knowledge, so the verse is not connected to what precedes it concerning the command to jihad. Rather, when Allah (glorified is He) explained the obligation of migration and jihad, and each of them is a journey for worship, after He had favoured jihad He mentioned the other journey, which is migration for the pursuit of knowledge. So the pronouns in "yatafaqqahu" and "yundhiru" refer to the company mentioned, namely the one going forth, and this is what the statement of Mujahid requires. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and others transmitted from him that he said: Some companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out into the desert, and they obtained from the people some kindness and some fertility by which they benefited, and they called those among the people whom they found to guidance. The people said to them: "We see you have only abandoned your companions and come to us." So they felt within themselves some discomfort at that, and they all came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed: ﴿It was not for the believers...﴾ and so on, that is: "If only a part went forth and a part remained behind, seeking good, that they may gain understanding in the religion, and that they may hear what has been revealed, and that they may warn the people when they return to them."

It has been used as evidence that gaining understanding in the religion is among the communal obligations (fard al-kifaya). As for what is in Kashf al-Hijab from Abu Sa'id: "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim," despite al-Saghani's weakening of it, the intended knowledge in it is only that upon which the performance of the obligations depends, and there is no doubt that learning it is an obligation upon every Muslim. Some mentioned that the verse contains an indication that the report of a single narrator (khabar al-ahad) is authoritative, because the generality of "every division" requires that from every three who are alone in a village a company should go forth to fiqh in order to warn their people, that they may remember and beware. So if the reports were not considered, unless they were mass-transmitted (mutawatir), this would not benefit. Some established the manner of the indication in two matters. The first: that Allah (exalted is He) commanded the company to warn, and this requires doing what is commanded, for otherwise it would not be warning. The second: His (glorified is He) command to the people to beware upon warning, because the meaning of His statement (exalted is He) ﴿that they may beware﴾ is "so that they may beware," and this too implies the obligation to act upon the report of a single narrator. This indication holds under either of the two interpretations you choose. The inference from the verse based on what has been mentioned does not depend on the company applying to a single person, who is the starting point of the preparation, but it suffices that it applies to what does not reach the level of mass transmission, even if they are three or more. Likewise, it does not depend on the hope not being from the warned, but rather it is from Allah (glorified is He), and what is meant by it is the demand, figuratively, as is not hidden.

[Page 50]

﴿O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are close to you﴾, i.e., those who are near you in physical proximity. He specified the command with this [verse], together with His saying, glorified is He, at the beginning of the surah, ﴿and kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, and similar verses. It was said: because it is known that it is impossible to fight all the disbelievers and to campaign against all the lands at one time, so whoever is nearer takes priority over whoever is farther. Also, abandoning the nearer and occupying oneself with fighting the farther does not guarantee safety from attacks on the offspring (dhurriyyah, i.e., women and children) and the weak. Also, the farther has no limit, unlike the nearer, so one is not commanded to [fight] it. And it may not be possible to fight the farther before fighting the nearer. Some of them said: the intended meaning is, fight the nearest, then the next nearest, until you reach the farthest, and by this the aim of fighting the polytheists in their entirety is achieved. So this is guidance to the way of achieving it in the most suitable manner.

From here, the Prophet (ﷺ) first fought his own people, then moved on to fight the rest of the Arabs, then to fight Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Khaybar and their like, then to fight the Romans. So the Prophet (ﷺ) began with fighting the nearest, then the next nearest, and his Companions followed his practice (ﷺ) until their expeditions (sara-ya) and armies reached what Allah, exalted is He, willed. Based on this, there is no naskh (abrogation). It is narrated from al-Hasan that the verse is abrogated by what preceded it, but the verifying scholars hold that there is no basis for this. Al-Khazin, following others, claimed that the intended meaning of "walī" (close ones) is that which includes both physical nearness and kinship nearness, but this is contrary to the apparent meaning. It was also said that it is specific to kinship nearness, because it was revealed when people felt reluctant to kill their relatives; but its weakness is not hidden.

﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., severity, as Ibn Abbas said. The word (ghilẓah) has three vowel forms for its ghayn (ghayn being vowelled in three ways), and it has been read in that way, but the seven [canonical readers] read it with a kasra. The intended meaning of severity includes boldness, steadfastness in fighting, and roughness in killing and taking captives, and the like. From here they said: it is a comprehensive word, and the command is in the manner of [the expression] "let me not see you here." So the intent is not to command the disbelievers to find that in the believers, but rather to command the believers to take on the qualities mentioned, so that the disbelievers find them possessing it. ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ (123), with protection and support. By "the righteous" is meant either those addressed, and the explicit mention is to specify that faith and fighting in the manner mentioned are from the category of piety, and a testimony to their being of the company of the righteous; or the category in general, and they are included in it at the first level of inclusion. Whichever it is, the statement is an explanatory justification (ta'līl) emphasizing what precedes it.

﴿When a surah is revealed﴾ from the surahs of the Qur'an, ﴿some of them﴾, meaning of the hypocrites, as reported from Qatadah and others, ﴿say﴾, in a manner of denial and mockery, to their companions in order to confirm them in hypocrisy, or to the weak among the believers in order to turn them away from faith: ﴿Which of you has this surah increased﴾ ﴿in faith﴾? ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read ﴿Ayyakum﴾ with a fatha, on the assumption of a verb implied by what is mentioned, which is to be understood as postponed, because the interrogative has precedence. The meaning is: "Which of you has the surah increased, so that it increased him?" and so on.

Regarding the increase, considering it in the first of the two possibilities, addressed to them, is in view of the belief of the believers. ﴿As for those who believed﴾ is a response from the side of Him, exalted is His majesty, and a confirmation of the truth and a specification of their state, both in the present and in the hereafter. Some of the scrupulous scholars said: the verse indicates that they are mockers and that their mockery is objectionable. So His saying, exalted is He, ﴿As for those who believed, and as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ comes as a detailing of these two categories. Al-Tibi made this a detailing of an omitted element and explained it in a way the heart does not incline to. Whatever the case, the response of ("idha", "when") is the clause ﴿So among them﴾ and what follows, and this is not a conjunction upon it. That is: ﴿As for those who believed﴾ in God, glorified is He, and in what came from Him, ﴿it has increased them in faith﴾, meaning in assent, because that is what is understood immediately from faith, as has been established in its proper place. As for the acceptance of assent itself to increase, decrease, intensity and weakness, this is what a group of the verifying scholars have held, and I say the same, due to the apparent meaning of the verses and reports, and even if the veil were lifted for me, I would not increase in certainty. Whoever does not accept that it admits of increase, and does not include deeds in faith, said: its increase is by the increase of its object and of what is believed in, and the words of Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, point to this. It was said: this entails that there would be no increase today, because the religion has been completed and no new object has renewed; but there is an issue with this, even if it was said by one whose eminence is counted on the fingers and in whose words hearts place their trust. As for the one who does not accept this and includes deeds in faith, increase and its opposite are evident to him. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ 124

at its revelation, because it is a cause of an increase in their perfection and an elevation of their ranks. Indeed, by my life, it is more beneficial than the scattering of the staff.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 125:

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, i.e., hypocrisy, ﴿it adds to them filth upon their filth﴾, i.e., hypocrisy added to their hypocrisy. The increase (al-ziyadah) here includes the meaning of addition (al-damm), and for this reason it is construed with ila (to). It has been said that ila here means ma'a (with), but there is no need for this (wa la hajata ilayhi).

﴿And they die while they are disbelievers﴾ [9:125]. That [condition] became firmly established in them until they die upon it.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 126:

﴿Do they not see﴾ meaning the hypocrites. The hamzah (الهمزة, the interrogative particle) here expresses rebuke and reproach, and the discussion of its placement relative to the conjunction (al-ʿatf, coordination) is well known. Hamzah, Ya'qub, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b read it with the second-person ta' (التاء الفوقانية), so that the address is to the believers, and the hamzah then expresses wonder, meaning: "Do they not know?" It is also said: "Do they not perceive?" ﴿that they﴾, i.e., the hypocrites, ﴿are tried every year﴾ of the years, ﴿once or twice﴾ by various kinds of afflictions, such as sickness and hardship, which remind them of their sins and of standing before the Knower of the unseen, and so lead them to faith in Him, the Exalted, and to restraining themselves from what they are upon. In a report: "When a servant falls ill and is then healed but does not increase in goodness, the angels say: 'This is the one whom we treated, but the medicine did not benefit him.'" So fitnah (الفتنة, trial or affliction) here means calamity and punishment. It is also said that it means testing, and the meaning is: "Do they not see that they are tested through jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so they witness the verses that are revealed to him, especially those that expose their ugly deeds, and then they repent of what they are engaged in?" ﴿Nor do they take heed﴾ and do not learn a lesson. The clause, according to the recitation of the majority, is a conjunction (ʿatf) of ﴿they see﴾, falling under the rebuke and reproach. According to the other recitation, it is a conjunction of ﴿they are tried﴾. What is meant by "once" and "twice," as some have stated, is merely multiplicity, not a precise statement of occurrence according to the specified number. Abdullah recited: "Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice, and yet they do not remember?"

Commentary of al-Alusi (*Ruh al-Ma'ani*) on surah 9, verse 127:

﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾ is an explanation of their state at its revelation, when they were in the gathering where the revelation was conveyed, just as the first clause explains their statements when they were absent from it. ﴿They look at one another﴾ in order to agree among themselves to flee, out of their dislike of listening to it, saying by gesture: ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾ That is, does any of the Muslims see you if you rise from the assembly? Or they wink with their eyes, mocking it and denying it, saying: "Does anyone see you?" so that they may leave, showing that they cannot endure listening to it, and laughter overcomes them so that they are exposed. According to this view, the surah is unrestricted. It has also been said that their looking at one another and their winking were out of rage at what the surah contained of their disgraceful acts and the exposure of their ugly deeds. Thus, the surah meant is a surah containing that. The unrestricted sense is the apparent one. In either case, it is necessary to supply a verb of saying before the interrogative so that the speech is connected. If it is taken as a noun, it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), as we indicated. If it is taken as a verb, the sentence is also in the position of a circumstantial clause. It is permissible to make it a new independent sentence. The use of the second-person pronoun is to urge the addressees toward resolve, for a person is more concerned with his own affair than with the affair of his companions, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let him be gentle and let no one become aware of you﴾. ﴿Then they turned away﴾ is conjoined to ﴿they look at one another﴾. The delay (*tarakhi*) is with regard to the existence of the opportunity and the ascertaining that none of the believers sees them. That is, then they all turned away from the gathering of revelation because they could not bear to hear that, due to their intense dislike, or from fear of exposure through overpowering laughter, or from being discovered in their winking, or they turned away from the assembly because of rage. It has also been said: the meaning is their turning away from guidance. The first is more apparent.

(﴿Allah has turned their hearts away from faith﴾) in accordance with their turning away from that assembly. The sentence may be informative or supplicatory, and Abu Muslim and others from the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school which holds that human acts are created by humans and that God's justice requires them to be free) chose the second. His supplication against His servants is a threat against them and an announcement that punishment will befall them. As for His words, glorified is He:
[Page 52]
﴿because they﴾: it has been said that it is connected to *sarafa* (turned away) on the first interpretation and to *inṣarafū* (turned away) on the second. The *ba'* is causal, meaning: because they are ﴿a people who do not comprehend﴾ (127), either due to the badness of their understanding or due to their failure to reflect. Thus they are either foolish or heedless.

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 128:**

﴿There has certainly come to you﴾: the address is to the Arabs. ﴿a Messenger﴾: that is, a Messenger of great standing. ﴿from among yourselves﴾: that is, of your own kind and of your own lineage, an Arab like yourselves. ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and others related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "There is no tribe among the Arabs but that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born to it: its Mudar, its Rabiʿah and its Yemenis."

It has also been said: the address is to mankind in general, and the meaning of his (ﷺ) being "from among yourselves" is that he is of the human species.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Muḥaysin and al-Zuhri read (anfasikum) [from anfas], an elative form (afʿal al-tafḍīl) from nafasah (preciousness), and the intended meaning is nobility. Thus he (ﷺ) was among the noblest of the Arabs. al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound, and al-Nasa'i related from al-Muṭṭalib ibn Rabiʿah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when word of some of what people were saying had reached him, mounted the pulpit, praised Allah the Exalted and extolled Him, and said: 'Who am I?' They said: 'You are the Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I am Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Allah the Exalted created the creation and placed me in the best of His creation; He made them into two groups and placed me in the best group; He made them into tribes and placed me in the best tribe; He made them into houses and placed me in the best house. So I am the best of you in house and the best of you in person.'" al-Bukhari and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalail related from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent forth from the best of the generations of the children of Adam, generation after generation, until I was of the generation in which I was."

Muslim and others related from Wathilah ibn al-Asqaʿ, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted chose Ismaʿil from the offspring of Ibrahim, chose from the offspring of Ismaʿil the Banu Kinanah, chose from the Banu Kinanah the Quraysh, chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and chose me from the Banu Hashim." al-Bayhaqi related from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people have ever split into two groups except that Allah placed me in the better of the two. I was brought forth from between my parents, and nothing of the immorality of the Jahiliyyah touched me. I came forth from a lawful marriage and not from illicit union, from Adam until I reached my father and mother. So I am the best of you in person and the best of you in father."

﴿grievous to him﴾: that is, hard and difficult, from ʿazza ʿalayhi, meaning it was hard and distressing to him. ﴿is your suffering﴾: that is, your distress (ʿanat), which is a disliked matter, meaning that what befalls you of hardship is grievous to him, such as an evil end and falling into punishment. The word ﴿ʿazīz﴾ is in the nominative as a descriptive qualifier (ṣifah sababiyyah) of ﴿rasūl﴾, and ﴿ʿalayhi﴾ is connected to it, its agent being the verbal noun; this is what the apparent sense of the sublime wording requires. It has also been said that ﴿ʿazīz ʿalayhi﴾ is a fronted predicate and ﴿mā ʿanittum﴾ is a postponed subject, and the clause is in the position of a qualifier. It has also been said that ﴿ʿazīz﴾ is a true adjective of ﴿rasūl﴾, and the sentence is complete at that point, and ﴿ʿalayhi mā ʿanittum﴾ begins a new sentence, meaning: your distress concerns him and is hard upon him.

﴿Eager over you﴾: that is, eager for your faith and the good of your affairs, because eagerness does not attach to their persons. ﴿for the believers﴾ among you and among others. ﴿Kind and merciful﴾ (128). It has been said: he placed the more emphatic of the two first, which is ra'fah, the term for intensity of mercy, in observance of the verse-endings (fawasil), and this is a consideration observed in the Qur'an. This is based on how ra'fah was explained. And he affirmed that ra'fah is tenderness (shafaqah) and raḥmah is beneficence (iḥsan). It may also be said: ra'fah is placed first in view of its effects being the repelling of harms, while raḥmah is placed later in view of its effects being the bringing of benefits; the former is more important than the latter. For this reason it is placed first in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they invented﴾. The consideration of verse-endings does not apply here, as is not hidden. It seems that on this basis ra'fah is derived from rafw al-thawb, mending a torn garment, so that his (ﷺ) being described with it means he is described as repelling harm from them and bringing them benefit. These two names were not gathered for anyone other than him (ﷺ). Some have claimed that the meaning is: kind to those of them who obey, merciful to those who sin. It has been said: kind to his kinsmen, merciful to his allies. It has been said: kind to whoever sees him, merciful to whoever does not see him. There is no basis for any of these.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 9, verse 129 (part 1 of 2):

﴿So if they turn away﴾: a shift from address (talwin) and a turning of the address toward him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as consolation for him. That is: if they turn away from believing in you, ﴿then say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, for He will suffice you against their harm and will help you against them. ﴿There is no deity but Him﴾: this is a resumed statement (isti'naf), serving as a proof for what precedes it, because the one singled out for divinity (al-uluhiyyah) is the one who suffices and helps. ﴿In Him I have put my trust﴾: so I neither hope nor fear except from Him, glorified is He. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Throne﴾, that is, the body that encompasses all other bodies, which is called the sphere of spheres (falak al-aflak) and is the limiter of directions (muhaddid al-jihat), ﴿the Mighty﴾, whose greatness none knows the measure of except Allah, exalted is He. In a report: "The earth, in comparison to the lowest heaven, is like a ring in a desert; and likewise the lowest heaven in comparison to the heaven above it, and so on up to the seventh heaven, which in comparison to the Kursi is like a ring in a desert, and the Kursi in comparison to the Throne is likewise." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that no one can estimate its measure. The astronomers have mentioned that the distance from the concave surface of the greatest sphere to the center of the universe is thirty-three million, five hundred and twenty-four thousand, six hundred and nine farsakh, and that the distance of its convex surface from it has reached a degree that none knows except Allah, to whom not an atom's weight in the earth or in the heaven is hidden, and He is Knowing of all things. The Throne here may be interpreted as sovereignty (al-mulk), which is one of its meanings as in the Qamus. It was also read "al-'Azim" in the nominative, as an attribute of the Lord. Allah concluded this surah with what He mentioned because He mentioned in it burdensome obligations and difficult admonitions, so He wished, majestic is His affair, to make that easy for them and to encourage the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in conveying it. He included in his noble attributes, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, what He included. He began with his being from among themselves, because he is like a mother in this regard. His being described, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with kindness and mercy toward the believers does not contradict his imposing upon them in this surah various kinds of burdensome obligations, because this imposition is also part of the perfection of that attribute, insofar as it is a means of escaping everlasting punishment and attaining everlasting reward. Of this kind is his dealing, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with the three who were left behind, as you know. How good is what has been said:

"He was harsh so that they would be restrained, and whoever is resolute, let him sometimes be harsh toward one who is merciful."

These two verses, according to what is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, are the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. However, al-Shaykhan related from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The last verse revealed is: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-kalalah﴾, and the last surah revealed is Bara'ah." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, the last verse revealed was ﴿And fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah﴾, and between its revelation and his death, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, there were eighty days; it was said nine nights. Some have tried to reconcile the reports on this matter in a way that is not free from difficulty. What is narrated from Ubayy is further weakened by what Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Medina, the Juhaynah came to him and said: 'You have settled among us, so give us a firm covenant that we may be secure from you and you from us.' He said: 'Why do you ask this?' They said: 'We seek security.' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you﴾..." etc. And Allah knows best the reality of the matter.

They have mentioned, regarding His saying ﴿So if they turn away﴾ and the verse, the special properties they mentioned. Abu Dawud recorded from Abu al-Darda', as a statement of his own (mawquf), and Ibn al-Sunni from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says, when he enters the morning and when he enters the evening: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity but Him; in Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne,' seven times, Allah will suffice him for whatever concerns him of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter." And Ibn al-Najjar recorded in his history from al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Whoever says in the morning seven times: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity but Him,' etc., no distress, calamity, or drowning will befall him on that day or that night." Abu al-Shaykh recorded from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: A detachment went out toward the land of the Romans, and a man among them fell and his thigh broke, and they could not carry him, so they tied his horse beside him and placed beside him some water and provisions. When they turned away, someone came to him and said: "What is wrong with you here?" He said: "My thigh has broken, and my companions have left me." He said: "Place your hand where you feel the pain and say: ﴿So if they turn away﴾ and the verse." He placed his hand and recited it, and he was healed, mounted his horse, and caught up with his companions. This verse is the litany (wird) of this humble one, and to Allah belongs praise; for years we have asked Allah to grant us goodness through its blessing, for He is the best of those who grant success.

* * *

Furthermore, from the realm of allusion (al-isharah) in the verses: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for them is Paradise﴾. When Allah, glorified is He, guided them to faith by knowledge, while they were captivated by love of self and wealth, He drew them down, out of the utmost care He has for them, from that through a profitable transaction, by giving them Paradise in exchange. Perhaps what is meant by it is the Paradise of the self, so that the price is of the same kind as the thing priced, which is what is familiar to them. But there is a difference between the two matters. Ibn 'Ata' said: "Your self is the locus of every desire and affliction, and your wealth is the place of every sin and disobedience, so your Master has purchased that from you in order to remove what harms you and to compensate you with what benefits you for it. For this reason He, glorified is He, purchased the self and did not purchase the heart." Some of the great ones have also mentioned on this matter that the self is the locus of defect, and the generous one desires to buy what others shun. So Allah's purchase of that, while He is aware of the defect, in exchange for Paradise, which has no defect, is the utmost generosity. What points to this is the saying of the poet:

"I have a liver full of sores; who will sell me for it a liver free of sores?
All people refuse to buy it, but whoever buys the diseased for the healthy..."

And from al-Junayd, may his secret be sanctified, who said: "He, glorified is He, purchased from you what is your attribute and under your control, while the heart is under His attribute and His control; the sale did not take place upon it." What points to this is his, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: "The heart of the son of Adam is between two fingers of the fingers of the Merciful." Some interpreters of the Qur'an have mentioned that when He purchased the selves from them, and they tasted, through detachment from them, the sweetness of certainty and the pleasure of renunciation, and they turned back from the station of the pleasure of the self and repented of its desires, and there remained with them no value for the Paradise of the self that was the price, He described them as the repentant, saying, glorified is He: ﴿The repentant﴾, that is, those who turn back from seeking the delights of the self and from expecting reward, toward Him, exalted is He. In other words, they are a people who have returned from other than Allah to Allah and have remained steadfast with Allah, exalted is He. ﴿The worshippers﴾, that is, the humble, those who abase themselves before His greatness and majesty, exalting and honoring Him, majestic is His affair, neither desiring reward nor fearing punishment. This is the highest degree of worship, and some call it the servitude of servanthood (ubudiyyah). ﴿The praisers﴾, by manifesting perfections, practical and cognitive, a praise that is active and states-based. The highest level of praise is the manifestation of inability to praise. It is reported that David, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, how can I praise You, when praise itself is one of Your blessings?" Allah revealed to him: "Now you have praised Me, O David." How sublime is the saying of our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "O Allah, I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself."

﴿The wanderers﴾ toward Him, exalted is He, by emigrating from the station of innate nature (fitrah) and seeing the perfections established for them in the deserts of attributes and the stations of the glorifications (al-sabahat). Some of the knowers have said: The wanderers are those who travel with their hearts in the dominion, flying with the wings of love in the air of majesty. It may also be said: they are those who fast from familiar things when they behold the crescent of His beauty in this creation, and do not break their fast until they behold Him once more in the next creation, and they have complied with what he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, alluded to in his saying: "Fast when you see it, and break your fast when you see it."

﴿The bowers﴾ in the station of the effacement of attributes, ﴿the prostrators﴾ through the annihilation of the essence. Some of the knowers have said: The bowers are the lovers, bent under the weight of the burdens of knowledge at the gate of greatness and the sight of awe, and the prostrators are the seekers of nearness to Him, glorified is He, for it has come in a report: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating." It may also be said: the bowers and prostrators are the witnesses of the Beloved, hearing from Him. How good is what has been said:

"If they heard as I heard her speech, they would fall down bowing and prostrating before Izzah."

﴿Those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾, that is, those who call creation to the Truth and repel them from anything other than It, for what is right in absolute terms is the Truth, glorified is He, and everything else is, in relation to Him, mighty of station, wrong. ﴿And those who guard the limits of Allah﴾, that is, those who observe His commands and prohibitions, glorified is He, in their limbs, their secrets, and their spirits; or those who have guarded the known limits of Allah and upheld them upon themselves and upon others. It was also said: they are those who stand in the station of servanthood after the unveiling of the attributes of lordship for them, so they do not transgress that; and even if what they experience occurs, they are in the station of establishment and sobriety, and do not say what the intoxicated of love say, nor wander in the valleys of ecstatic utterances.

In the verse there is a rebuke of people who claimed to belong to the party of Allah and the company of His friends, while they had neglected the limits, broken the ship of the Sharia, and spoken false words before the Muslims of all their sects, even before the Sufi masters, for they made the observance of the stations obligatory, and said:

"Neglecting them is heresy; I have mixed with them, and I have seen from them abominations; by the Guardian, we seek refuge."

By my life, the believer is one who denounces such people, so beware of being deceived by them. ﴿And give good news to the believers﴾ of true faith, who abide in the station of uprightness and following the Sharia. ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Hellfire﴾, that is: it was not correct for them nor proper; for standing at the decree is the way of the perfected.

From this it is said: the aspiration of the knower ('arif, one who knows God) has no effect after the perfection of his gnosis (irfan). That is, when he is certain that everything occurs by the decree of the Exalted, which accords with perfect wisdom, and that what Allah wills comes to be and what He does not will does not come to be, and when he does not accuse Allah, glorified is He, of anything in doing or in leaving undone, he settles under the shelter of the decrees. He submits to the claimant of will and listens to the caller of wisdom, and he leaves his own desire for the desire of the Beloved. Indeed, he wills nothing except what He wills. This is what the station of pure servanthood ('ubudiyya mahda) requires, and it is the highest of the stations. Below it is the station of idlal (intimate, familiar presumption before the Beloved).

Our master, the axis of the divine (al-Qutb al-Rabbani), Shaykh Abd al-Qadir al-Kilani, may Allah sanctify his secret, was in this station. He has words that point to this. However, he did not die until he had moved from it to the station of pure servanthood, as Mawlana Abd al-Wahhab al-Sha'rani related in al-Durar wal-Yawaqit. He also mentioned that this station was the station of his disciple, our master Abu al-Su'ud al-Shalabi, may Allah sanctify his secret.

﴿And Allah would not lead a people astray﴾: that is, would not describe them as astray from the path of submission, surrender to His command, and contentment with His judgment, ﴿after He had guided them﴾ to the knowledge-based tawhid (tawhid 'ilmi) and to seeing that everything occurs by His decree and destiny, ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should guard against﴾: that is, what it is obligatory for them to guard against at every station of their journey and every rank of their arrival. So when He makes that clear to them, if they proceed in some of the stations to what has been made clear to them as obligatory to guard against, He leads them astray for committing what is error in their religion. Otherwise, not. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾: so He knows the subtleties of their sins even if no one perceives them.

﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾. It is not hidden that the repentance (tawba) of Allah, glorified is He, toward each of the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, and those with him is according to his station. Some have said that when tawba is attributed to the servant, it means returning from misdeeds to acts of obedience. When it is attributed to Allah, glorified is He, it means His returning to the servants with the attribute of union (wisal), the opening of the door, and the lifting of the veil.

﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind, until when the earth was narrow for them despite its vastness, and their souls confined them﴾: this was because they sensed the displeasure of the Beloved. ﴿And they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾: that is, they realized this, so they cut off [all else] and turned to Him, glorified is He, ﴿and they abandoned intermediaries﴾. ﴿Then He turned to them [in forgiveness]﴾, since He saw their detachment toward Him and their humbling before Him. The custom of the Exalted with the people of His love is that when something proceeds from them that contradicts their station through a lapse of adab, He veils them in some form, until they taste the bitterness of the transgression and are veiled from witnessing. Whatever befalls them of that which makes them forget their worldly life and their hereafter, He then showers upon them the heavy rain of the cloud of generosity, and He illuminates the horizons of their secrets with the lights of eternity. So He comforts them after their despair and bestows favor upon them after their despondency. ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired﴾. How sweet is his saying:

They abandoned, while desire is union and separation, and so is the way of the charming passion.

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾ in all vices by abstaining from them, ﴿and be with the truthful﴾ in intention, speech and action; that is, characterize yourselves with what they are characterized by of truthfulness. It has been said: associate with them so that you become like them, for every companion is imitated through association. Some have interpreted "the truthful" as those who did not break the first covenant, for it is the truest word. It may be said: the origin is truthfulness in the covenant of Allah, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have fulfilled what they pledged to Allah﴾. Then [truthfulness is required] in the binding of resolve and the promise to creation, as He, glorified is He, said about Isma'il: ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾. When truthfulness is observed in all places, such as the thought, the reflection, the intention, the speech and the deed, then the dreams, the inspirations, the states, the stations, the gifts and the witnessings become true. It is the root of the tree of perfection, the seed of the fruit of states, and the foundation of every good and happiness. Its opposite is lying, which is the worst and ugliest of vices, and it contradicts manliness (muruwwa), as they say: there is no manliness for a liar.

﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a group from every division of them go forth that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾. This is an indication that it is obligatory for every capable group to take the path of seeking knowledge, since it is not possible for all of them to do so. Outwardly this is because of the loss of benefits; inwardly it is because not all are prepared for it. The fiqh (understanding of the religion) is among the sciences of the heart. It is only attained through purification (tazkiya), refinement (tasfiya), leaving aside what is habitual, and following the Shari'a. So the going forth here means the spiritual journey (safar ma'nawi). This is beneficial knowledge, and its sign is that one fears no one other than Allah, the Exalted. Do you not see how Allah denied fiqh to those who feared other than Him, saying: ﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾?

On this basis, it is right that someone like me should lament over himself. Some of the great scholars have declared that fiqh is a knowledge firmly rooted in the heart, its roots fixed in the soul, its effect evident upon the limbs, such that its possessor cannot commit an act contrary to what it requires, except when qada' (divine decree) and qadar overcome him. It is said that Allah, the Exalted, revealed to one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, peace be upon them: "Do not say, 'Who will bring knowledge down from the heavens?' nor 'Who will ascend to the depths of the earth to bring it?' nor 'Who will cross the sea to bring it?' Knowledge is placed in your hearts. Adorn yourselves before Me with the adab of the spiritual beings, and take on the character of the truthful. I will make knowledge manifest from your hearts until it overwhelms and covers you." It is also reported: "Whoever fears Allah for forty mornings, springs of wisdom gush forth from his heart." When you have verified this, you will know that the claim of the people of today to fiqh in the sense we have mentioned, together with their rushing into sins like moths rushing into fire and their forming circles around them, is a false claim that contradicts both reason and transmission. Far is it that such fiqh would be attained by them so long as they remain in that state, even if they struck their heads against a thousand solid rocks.

His, glorified is He, joining His saying: ﴿and warn their people when they return to them﴾ to His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding﴾ indicates that warning comes after understanding and adornment with virtues, since it is that from which benefit is hoped:

Begin with yourself and restrain it from its error; when it desists from it, then you are wise.

Then there it will hear what you say, and be followed, and instruction will benefit.

Hence the Majestic and Exalted said: ﴿that they may beware﴾. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you﴾

(indication of the greater jihad). Perhaps this is an instruction on how the desired victory is to be achieved, and an explanation of the way of attaining fiqh. That is: fight the disbelieving forces of your souls by opposing their desires. It is reported: "The enemy most hostile to you is your soul that is between your two sides."

﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾: that is, subjugation and severity, until you reach the degree of taqwa. ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ by wilaya and victory. ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾: that is, He afflicts them with trials so that they may repent. ﴿Then they do not repent, nor do they remember﴾. It is reported: "Trial is one of the whips of Allah, the Exalted, by which He drives His servants toward Him." This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾. In sum, trial breaks the fury of the soul, so the heart softens and turns to its Master. However, whoever is overcome by wretchedness loses that state when the trial is turned away from him, as His saying indicates: ﴿Then when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾, and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So when We removed his harm, he passed on as though he had never called Us concerning a harm that had touched him﴾.

﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾: that is, from your own kind, so that affection may be established between you and him, for kind inclines to kind. Then it becomes easy for you to draw from his lights, may Allah, the Exalted, bless him and grant him peace. It is recited as we have mentioned: (مِن أنْفَسِكُمْ) that is, the most honorable of you in every respect. It suffices for his nobility that he, upon him be prayers and peace, is the first of the determinations (ta'ayyunat), and that, as Allah, the Exalted, described him, he is "upon a tremendous character."

And though his describers vary in describing him, time passes while there remains what has not been described.

﴿Grievous to him is what you suffer﴾: that is, your hardship weighs heavily upon him, upon him be prayers and peace, so he suffers, may Allah, the Exalted, bless him and grant him peace, at what pains you, as a person suffers when something disagreeable afflicts one of his limbs. It is reported from Sahl that he said: the meaning is that your heedlessness of Allah, the Exalted, even for the blink of an eye, is grievous to him. For (العَنَت) is that which is hard, and in reality nothing is harder than heedlessness of the Beloved. ﴿Ardently desirous of you﴾: that is, for the rectification of your affairs, or for your presence and for your not being heedless of your Master, majestic is His glory. ﴿Toward the believers, Kind and Merciful﴾: ﴿Kind (ra'uf)﴾ repels from them what harms them, and ﴿Merciful (rahim)﴾ brings to them what benefits them. Among the effects of kindness is his warning them against sins and transgressions, and among the effects of mercy is his bestowing upon them knowledge, gnosis and perfections, may Allah, the Exalted, bless him and grant him peace.

Ja'far al-Sadiq, may Allah, the Exalted, be pleased with him, said: Allah, the Exalted, knew the incapacity of His creation to obey Him, so He made them know this, so that they would know that they would not attain purity of service to Him. So He, glorified is He, placed between Himself and them a created being of their own kind in form, and He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾. He clothed him with the attribute of kindness and mercy, and sent him forth to creation as a truthful emissary, and made obedience to him and agreement with him as agreement with Him. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾. Then He singled him out for Himself alone, and drew him to Himself by witnessing him in all his breaths. And He consoled his heart concerning their turning away from following him by His saying, majestic is His glory: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they turn away from accepting what you are upon, due to lack of readiness and its loss, ﴿then say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾: I have no need of you, just as a person has no need of a rotting limb which, by reason, must be cut off. Allah, the Exalted, is sufficient. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾: so there is no effective agent other than Him, and no helper besides Him. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾: not upon any other of all created beings, since I see no act, no power and no strength in any of them except by Allah. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾, which encompasses all things. He, glorified is He, clothed it with the lights of His majesty and strengthened it to bear His manifestations. Were it not so, it would melt in less than the blink of an eye. If (العَظِيمِ) is read in the nominative, it is an attribute of the Lord, glorified is He, and His majesty, exalted is His grandeur, has no limit. ﴿And they did not appraise Allah with His true appraisal﴾. We ask Him, by His majesty and His greatness, to grant us success in completing the tafsir of His Book as He loves and is pleased with. There is no deity but Him, and none is hoped for but His goodness.
